key_insight: Intensity-modulated photoluminescence spectroscopy (IMPLS) measures perovskite charge-carrier lifetime at a defined operating injection level, and can separate lifetime from interface-transfer effects in complex stacks and devices.
engineering_relevance: IMPLS offers a frequency-domain, operando diagnostic that is directly relevant for benchmarking perovskite films, interface engineering, and solar-cell performance under realistic illumination.
method: Measure photoluminescence response under modulated excitation at one-sun-equivalent or other defined injection levels.
Fit the frequency response with a transfer function to disentangle charge transfer from interface recombination.
Compare IMPLS signatures with IMVS to reveal an additional frequency component that resolves the actual carrier lifetime.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement between IMPLS and steady-state photoluminescence lifetimes on thin films, plus a clear third frequency in devices where IMVS often fails because of capacitive effects.
watch_item: IMPLS in perovskite/transport-layer stacks requires careful transfer-function modeling, since the measured response mixes charge transfer, interface recombination, and true lifetime.
paper_title: Operando Charge Carrier Dynamics by Intensity-Modulated Photoluminescence: From Perovskite Thin Films to Solar Cells
